description: Batch-parallel BLOCKED Householder QR in Triton, attacking the trailing-update GEMM throughput that geqrf's 90%-unblocked-panel kernel wastes. Custom Triton kernel factors each width-~32-64 column panel across all batched matrices (compute V below-diag + tau + R on-diag), then apply the blocked update A -= V @ (T @ (V^T @ A)) as batched bf16/tf32 tensor-core GEMMs (torch.bmm or Triton) with fp32 accumulation. fp32-correct first, then bf16 trailing for the bulk. Output compact (H,tau); route off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Target dominant B=640 n=512.

Single-launch PERSISTENT fused QR megakernel in Triton to kill geqrf's ~55k-launch overhead. Launch ONE grid for the whole batch (a persistent set of CTAs, multiple CTAs cooperating per matrix — do NOT hold a full 512x512 fp32 tile in one CTA's smem, that exceeds sm_120's 228KB), looping column-panels with on-chip smem staging of the active panel + block-level sync, so an entire batched factorization is one or a few launches instead of tens of thousands. Output compact (H,tau); route off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Best for n<=512; targets launch-bound small-n wide-batch shapes.

CholeskyQR2 + Householder-reconstruction QR: a GEMM/tensor-core-dominant algorithm replacing per-panel reflector recurrence with big matmuls. Per matrix compute G=A^T@A (Triton/bmm), R=chol(G), Q=A@R^-1, repeat once (CholeskyQR2) for orthogonality, then RECONSTRUCT compact (H,tau) from (Q,R) via Householder so the output matches geqrf's contract and passes the gates. Must stay accurate on the guards' ill-conditioned rankdef/clustered/nearrank batches (fall back per-matrix to a Householder/geqrf path when chol fails, dispatching on numerics NOT conditioning-guessing). Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Targets compute-bound large n=1024/2048/4096.

Two-level NESTED blocking on your fused megakernel to shrink the trailing update that is still ~80% of n=512 time. Factor a WIDE super-panel (W~64-128) built from narrow inner panels (PB~16-32), accumulating a wide block reflector (V_wide, T_wide), then apply ONE fat trailing update A -= V_wide @ (T_wide @ (V_wide^T @ A)) as large fp32 GEMMs across the whole batch - far fewer, fatter trailing GEMMs and launches than the current per-PB update. Keep fp32 (mixed precision is worker 0's lane); hold the tight factor/orth gates on ill-conditioned shapes. Output compact (H,tau); off-grid n routes to geqrf. Target B=640 n=512 and B=60 n=1024.

TSQR / communication-avoiding panel factorization to break the panel kernel that is now your bottleneck (46% of n=512, 73% of n=4096), fixing all three pains you profiled: the 100KB SRAM wall, the sequential per-column BLAS-2 recurrence, and one-CTA-per-matrix occupancy starvation at n=4096 B=2. Partition the m panel rows into independent row-tiles; each CTA factors its small tile with ZERO cross-CTA sync (sidestepping Triton 3.6's lack of grid.sync), then a log-depth reduction tree merges the per-tile R factors (expressible as 2-3 hazard-free producer/consumer launches: leaf-factor, then tree-merge). Reconstruct compact (H,tau) from the TSQR factors so the geqrf contract + tight factor/orth gates hold on ill-conditioned shapes. Keep fp32 (mixed precision is your already-explored lane); off-grid n routes to geqrf. Targets tall n=2048/4096 and the dominant n=512.

Fuse the trailing-update GEMM chain (now ~42% of n=512 after the panel is squeezed). Collapse the three trailing matmuls V^T@A -> W=T^T@(.) -> A-=V@W into ONE Triton kernel that keeps the W intermediate in SRAM/registers instead of round-tripping HBM, cutting both launch count and the n*W intermediate traffic. Also fold the V-extraction (triu/tril split, 2.7%) and form_T (trsm, 4.7%) into the panel kernel's epilogue so per-panel launches drop further. Optionally overlap panel(k+1)'s leaf factor with trailing-update(k) (independent once V_k is known). Keep fp32 (mixed precision is your mapped dead-end); compact (H,tau); off-grid n -> geqrf. Targets the dominant B=640 n=512 and B=60 n=1024.

Break the fp32 wall with a LOW-PRECISION blocked-Householder panel + an fp32 CORRECTION step - the one axis nobody has cracked (worker 0 only tried low precision WITHOUT correction and failed the ill-cond gates). Factor panels/trailing in bf16/fp16 (fp8 only if margin allows) on tensor cores, then restore accuracy with a standard mixed-precision technique: CGS2 (classical Gram-Schmidt twice) OR one Newton-Schulz re-orthogonalization step Q<-Q(1.5I-0.5 Q^T Q) to drive ||Q^TQ-I|| down, plus one fp32 residual correction on R. The low-precision factor only needs to be a good preconditioner, not accurate; one fp32 pass contracts the rowscale/nearrank backward-error blowups quadratically. Reuse your reconstruction/refinement expertise to keep output compact (H,tau). Hold the tight gates (20/100 n eps32) on ALL ill-cond guard shapes; per-matrix numerical fallback to geqrf only on detected failure, not conditioning-guessing. Off-grid n -> geqrf. Mandate bf16/fp16 first, fp8 only if it still passes. Target the dominant B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024 where the board #1 (~1293us, mxfp-style) lives.

Port two techniques INTO your resident megakernel (not a code-merge - the layouts differ; transfer the ideas). PRIMARY: replace your serial larft build-T (25% of time) with the CLOSED-FORM block reflector T = inv(triu(V^T V,1) + diag(1/tau)) computed once per super-panel - worker 0 got a big win from this via one solve_triangular; do the equivalent inside your fused structure (small WxW solve, W=64). SECONDARY: your trailing is 53% and HBM-bandwidth-bound, so bf16x3 (split-fp32) accumulation in the fat wide-block trailing tl.dot MIGHT finally pay now that the block is fat (M,N,K all large per super-panel) - you found tf32x3 slower than ieee, but bf16x3 on fat blocks is a different regime; measure it, keep only if it passes the ill-cond gates AND beats fp32. Stay on your single-CTA resident structure (do NOT adopt worker 0's torch.bmm trailing - it would destroy your smem residency). Keep compact (H,tau), off-grid n + n>=2048 -> geqrf. This is distinct from worker 2's low-precision-FACTOR lane (you keep an fp32-accurate factor; only T-build and trailing-accumulate change). Target B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024.

Build the bf16/fp16-GEMM PRECONDITIONER pipeline you validated in prototype - the real precision frontier where tensor cores dominate cost (board #1 ~1293us is low-precision). Per matrix: cheap LOW-PRECISION QR (bf16/fp16 Gram or panel) -> Rlo (needs NO accuracy, just a preconditioner); M = A @ Rlo^-1 is then well-conditioned; run fp32 CholeskyQR2 on M (your already-built shifted-CholeskyQR + Triton diag-LU machinery from brief-0); reconstruct compact (H,tau) via orhr_col. The key: the bf16 tensor-core GEMMs (Gram A^T A, the M-form) are where the speed comes from, and they tolerate low precision because Rlo only preconditions. Per-matrix numerical fallback to geqrf on detected failure (chol info / NaN / cheap norm proxy), NOT conditioning-guessing. Mandate fp16 preconditioner (you found bf16 too coarse for the preconditioner itself - but bf16 is fine for the well-conditioned CholeskyQR2 Grams). Hold the tight factor+orth gates on ALL ill-cond shapes (rankdef/clustered/nearrank/rowscale/upper). Off-grid n -> geqrf. Target B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024 where the low-precision leaders live; this is distinct from worker 1's fp32-Householder lane.

Bring n>=2048 (n=2048, n=4096) INTO your fused kernel, off the geqrf fallback. After 25x on everything else, those two shapes - still running unoptimized geqrf (baseline ~75ms n=2048, ~51ms n=4096) - are now a dominant fraction of the geomean by Amdahl. Extend your panel-parallel nested-blocked Householder to large n: the challenge is the trailing matrix no longer fits one CTA's smem at n=4096, so use your multi-CTA trailing-update grid (already batch x tiles) across the wide trailing region, and tune super-panel width / tile counts for the tall-skinny regime. n=4096 has tiny batch (B=2) so per-matrix work must spread across many CTAs to fill the GPU - the panel-factor is the risk (one-CTA-per-matrix starves at B=2; consider a cooperative or geqrf-only-for-the-panel hybrid while doing the trailing in-kernel). Keep compact (H,tau), hold factor/orth gates on ill-cond shapes, fp32. Only fall back to geqrf for off-grid n. Primary target: n=2048 and n=4096.

The precision frontier (board #1 ~1293us is mxfp10): a GEMM-centric Householder where the TRAILING UPDATE is ONE LARGE fp16 GEMM at FULL trailing width - NOT worker 1's small-K (K=64) tl.dot tiles (that's why precision only bought 9% there). fp16 halves the T/WY buffer so re-block to WIDE super-panels (W=128, which OOM'd in fp32) making the trailing GEMM big enough that fp16 tensor cores finally pay 2x. Correct the FACTOR RESIDUAL (the only thing low precision degrades - Q from householder_product is always exactly orthogonal): recompute R=triu(Q^T A) once in fp32 (one GEMM, amortized over n/W panels). CRITICAL geomean guard: ill-conditioned matrices must fall back to fp32-trailing IN-KERNEL (same kernel, precision flag), NEVER to geqrf - 2 of 4 dominant n=512 bench shapes are rankdef/clustered, and routing those to geqrf's 117ms baseline would collapse the geomean. Detect per-matrix failure numerically (factor-residual proxy / NaN), not conditioning-guessing. geqrf only for off-grid n + n>=2048 (worker 1 owns large-n). Compact (H,tau). Target the dominant B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024.

FROM-SCRATCH large-tile frontier kernel - the only path to the mxfp10 board #1 (~1293us). Your 3 negatives proved the current small-K kernels top out; the unlock is W>=128 made COMPUTE-BOUND. Two concrete fixes to your prior dead-ends: (1) TILE the closed-form nilpotent-T construction so the [W,W] fp32 T-tile NEVER fully materializes in smem (that OOM, not trailing precision, is what blocked W=128). T is strictly-upper / nilpotent (Neumann-doubling, worker 1's form), so compute it column-panel by column-panel keeping only the active [W,b] sub-panel resident, stream the rest. This makes the wide trailing GEMM big enough that fp16/mxfp tensor cores genuinely pay ~2x+ (vs the 10-16% small-K gave). (2) Correct the FACTOR residual PER-PANEL incrementally in fp32 (refine each diagonal panel's R-block using the V^T A you already compute in-kernel) - O(panel), NOT the O(geqrf) global R=triu(Q^T A) that ballooned to 19x last time; never form global Q. Ill-cond matrices stay in-kernel via your validated fp32-trailing fallback (NEVER geqrf for n=512 - geomean trap). Compact (H,tau); tight gates on all ill-cond shapes; geqrf only off-grid + n>=2048. Target dominant B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024. This is a multi-hour bold rewrite - be ambitious.

COMBINE for the biggest remaining lever: large-n. By marginal log-analysis the geomean is now dragged by n=2048 (~1.1x) and n=4096 (~1x, still pure geqrf) while everything else is 25-60x - lifting n=4096 even to ~10x is worth more than any n<=1024 tweak. Worker 1 proved large-n is PANEL-FACTORIZATION-bound (~83% geqrf panel). You own BOTH ingredients: your brief-1 TSQR row-tiled LEAF factor (b71e4597 - fast, 183us/2560 tiles, fixes the tall-skinny low-batch occupancy starvation that one-CTA-per-matrix hits at n=4096 B=2) AND your brief-2 fused trailing + closed-form/Gram-T leader (79b357ff, 29.4x). Stack them: use the TSQR-style row-tiled panel factor for the n>=2048 panel (replacing geqrf's geqr2_smem_domino panel), feed its V/tau into your fused multi-CTA trailing update. The TSQR reconstruction overhead that killed it standalone is moot here - you're using the LEAF FACTOR for speed, not the HR reconstruction. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates on ill-cond. n<=1024 keeps your current 29.4x path; only n>=2048 changes. NO cuda streams (banned). Target n=2048 and n=4096.

COMBINE worker 0's 29.4x fused-trailing leader (79b357ff) with your closed-form nilpotent-T structure (0602a1e8) to push the dominant n=512/n=1024 past 29.4x. Worker 0's wins that you can fuse with yours: (1) read V IMPLICITLY from H in the trailing kernel - drops the materialized V tensor + both triu/tril kernels + the diagonal index-set + the VtV bmm; (2) fold form_T into a single fused Gram+T kernel; (3) R=32 narrow panel now beats R=64 post-fusion (fits SRAM unspilled, cheap fused trailing pays for extra panels). Worker 0's profile: n=512 panel dropped to 29%, fused trailing now 61% and SRAM-bound. Your DISTINCT asset is the nilpotent repeated-squaring closed-form T (ceil(log2 W) tensor-core matmuls, no larft recurrence, rank-deficient-safe via diag(tau)) and your single-CTA residency. See if your closed-form-T + worker 0's implicit-V/fused-Gram-T + R=32 beats 3999us - either by porting their fusion into your resident kernel, or porting your nilpotent-T into their kernel, whichever wins. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates, no cuda streams. Target B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024.

The board-#1 mechanism you have NOT tried: genuine fp8 (E4M3) / mxfp4 trailing - NOT fp16/bf16/tf32 (all capped). On sm_120 fp8 tensor cores are ~4x fp32 / ~2x fp16, and that DOUBLED headroom changes the correction calculus that capped your fp16 work: at 2x any full correction erased the win, but at 4x a SELECTIVE fp32 recompute of only the few unstable columns can fit inside the margin. Fork off worker 0's 29.4x fused-kernel leader (79b357ff - it already has bf16x3 fusion + BN/BM/warp tuning, the right base). Apply fp8/mxfp to the wide trailing GEMM (V^T@A and A-=V@W). CRITICAL: the per-matrix/per-column failure detector MUST be a pivot-growth / column-norm-ratio signal computed FROM THE fp8 TRAILING UPDATE ITSELF (max|update| vs running panel-norm), never |diag R| (that's conditioning-guessing, forbidden + invariance-guard-risky). Bound the selective fp32 recompute to a SMALL fraction of columns or it collapses to your brief-3 negative (full correction = full cost). mxfp block-scaling (per-block e8m0 scale) is the key to making fp8 pass the dynamic range of rowscale/clustered. Hold the tight factor+orth gates on ALL ill-cond shapes; geqrf only for truly-singular matrices detected legitimately + off-grid + n>=2048. Compact (H,tau). Target dominant B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024 toward mxfp10's 1293us. This closes the precision frontier either way - a clean fp8 negative lets the run stop spending on precision.

Holistic LAUNCH-COUNT reduction on the 32.8x leader - the precision frontier is closed (bf16x3 optimal on sm_120; 1293us is B200-only), so remaining wins are structural, and launch/python-dispatch overhead is the untapped one. The small/mid shapes (n=32 b=20, n=176 b=40, n=352 b=40) are almost certainly launch-overhead-bound not compute-bound: at n=32 the GPU work is trivial yet you pay per-launch dispatch across n/W super-panels x (panel-factor + Gram+T + trailing) kernels. Collapse per-super-panel launches into one mega-launch where the ~100KB smem permits (generous at small n), hoist invariant python-side setup out of the per-panel loop, and batch/fuse torch-level ops to cut python dispatch. You own this kernel's launch structure - it's your turf. NO cuda streams (banned, even in comments). Stay OFF worker 1's hot n<=1024 fused-combine MATH (it's actively improving that); you're attacking launch COUNT/overhead, a distinct axis. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold all gates. Target the small/mid shapes + any per-launch savings that also help n=512/1024.

RECURSIVE / divide-and-conquer panel factorization (Elmroth-Gustavson) - a genuinely DIFFERENT kernel structure from worker 0's left-looking fused trailing and worker 1's nested single-CTA, to expose more parallelism for the dominant wide-batch n=512. Recursively split each panel: factor the left half, update the right half with the left's block reflector, factor the right half, combine T factors. This trades the serial per-column BLAS-2 recurrence (the panel-factor floor everyone hit) for GEMM-rich recursive updates that tensor cores like, and the recursive T-accumulation is precision-sensitive (your numerical depth applies). The win is a faster PANEL FACTORIZATION via recursion-exposed parallelism, distinct from the trailing-update lane. Reconstruct compact (H,tau) matching geqrf. Hold the tight factor+orth gates on ALL ill-cond shapes (recursive combine must stay numerically stable on rankdef/clustered/nearrank). NO conditioning-based control flow (invariance guard - no tau=0 data-dependent skipping). fp32 (precision is closed). Off-grid n + n>=2048 -> geqrf. Target dominant B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024. This is a fresh structural algorithm - be bold; if recursion beats the current panel floor it compounds with the existing fast trailing.

Attack the trailing SRAM-traffic (69.7% of n=512, SRAM-bound) by RE-ORDERING the contraction so the skinny M=R=32 is no longer the GEMM's M. The update A -= V @ (T^T @ (V^T @ A)) is 3 matmuls; only the OUTER V@(.) carries M=R=32. Restructure the outer rank-R back-application so the TRAILING COLUMNS OF A (hundreds wide at n=512) are the M dimension and R=32 is the contraction K: a fat-M / skinny-K GEMM. Stage the R x (trailing) correction in SRAM ONCE and stream A's columns through, cutting the repeated re-read of A that dominates the 70%. This is pure loop-order/tiling inside YOUR trailing kernel - no wider R (that OOMs build-T + collides with worker 2's recursive panel), no batch-merge (block-diagonal dead-end, each V distinct). Realistic headroom is single-digit-% (it cuts A-rereads, not FLOPs - trailing is memory-bound) but it's the last credible trailing win before speed-of-light. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates, NO cuda streams. DISTINCT from worker 0 (launch-count) and worker 2 (recursive panel). Target B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024.

COMBINE for the highest remaining geomean leverage: route n>=2048 to CholeskyQR. In a geomean every shape has equal log-weight, and n=4096 (b=2, cond=1) is STILL ~1x (pure geqrf ~50ms) and n=2048 (b=8, cond=1) only ~6x - by far the worst two shapes. They're stuck because the Householder PANEL starves at tiny batch B=2/B=8 (too few matrices to fill the GPU). CholeskyQR is GEMM-bound: G=A^T A is one huge 4096x4096-scale tensor-core GEMM that fills the GPU even at B=2. Worker 2 already BUILT a CholeskyQR3 + orhr_col compact-(H,tau) reconstruction that passes ALL gates incl ill-conditioned (parent 48f95455) - integrate it as the n>=2048 path ONLY, keep your 34.6x fused Householder for n<=1024. Use shifted-CholeskyQR2 (cond=1 is mild; 2 passes likely enough, drop to 1 only if a gate margin demands). Per-matrix fallback to geqrf on DETECTED cholesky breakdown (info!=0) - that's reacting to measured failure, NOT conditioning-guessing, and N-dispatch is endorsed by the off-grid guard, so both are invariance-guard-safe. Expect real 6-10x on n=4096, 3-4x on n=2048. Compact (H,tau), hold all gates, NO cuda streams. Target n=2048 and n=4096.

JOINT multi-axis co-tune for n=512/1024 - the move you scoped: single-axis changes regress neighbors because the leader's R=32 components are tightly co-tuned, so change them TOGETHER. Build a from-scratch R=64 configuration sweeping ALL coupled axes jointly: (a) your recursive/2-level panel (which you proved is 1.3x faster standalone at R=64), (b) a fused in-kernel gram_T that works AT R=64 (the leader's gram_T falls back to cuBLAS solve_triangular above R=32 - extend the nilpotent closed-form T to R=64 in-kernel, it's ceil(log2 64)=6 squarings), and (c) a re-tuned trailing tile (BN/BM/num_warps) for the R=64 regime. The hypothesis: R=64 halves the panel COUNT (fewer trailing passes) and the 2-level panel makes the wider panel-factor affordable, IF gram_T and trailing are re-tuned for R=64 so they don't regress. Watch the ~100KB smem wall (your recurring limit) - if the fully-fused single-CTA R=64 panel OOMs, use a 2-CTA or split-panel staging rather than abandoning. Compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates, NO conditioning dispatch, NO cuda streams. DISTINCT from worker 1 (large-n CholeskyQR) and worker 0 (launch-count). Target B=640 n=512 + B=60 n=1024. This needs the multi-axis joint sweep, not one knob at a time.

DEVICE-SIDE software pipelining of the trailing-update tl.dot - a layer nobody has touched. Fork off worker 0's current 37.4x best (a4d9a6e4). Wrap the trailing kernel's K-loop (V^T@A and A-=V@W) in a software-pipelined tl.range(..., num_stages=N) and prefetch the next A/V tile via async cp.async copy, overlapping global-load latency with tensor-core compute. This is DISTINCT from worker 0's HOST-side launch overhead (python/torch.empty/num_warps at the call boundary) - num_stages is device-side instruction scheduling INSIDE the kernel body, tuned independently of num_warps. The trailing is memory-latency-exposed (the forced A re-read from the 100KB-SRAM two-pass structure is exactly the latency cp.async hides - pipelining attacks latency, not bandwidth, so target the A-reload stall specifically). Sweep num_stages 2/3/4 on the n=512 AND n=1024 trailing (nobody has pipelined n=1024 - 3 of 12 shapes, may have its own sweet spot). Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates, NO cuda streams.
